question.problem: If $[a]_{n}$ denotes the residue class containing all integers congruent to $a$ modulo $n,$ then $[-21]_{6}=$
question.worked_solution:
We have $[a]_{6}=[b]_{6}$ if 

$$
a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,6).
$$

The residue class $[-21]_{6}$ consists of the elements that are congruent to $-21$ modulo $6.$ 

We can find an alternative representation for this residue class as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[-21]_{6} & =\{x\in Z\,|\,x≡-21\,(\text{mod}\,6)\} \\  & =\{x\in Z\,|\,x≡(-4)\cdot 6+3\,(\text{mod}\,6)\} \\  & =\{x\in Z\,|\,x≡(-4)\cdot 0+3\,(\text{mod}\,6)\} \\  & =\{x\in Z\,|\,x≡3\,(\text{mod}\,6)\} \\  & =[3]_{6}\end{aligned}
$$
